title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-24
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a solid soundstage (minor mix quirks) captures an early‑'69 showcase highlighted by a stellar New Potato Caboose bass solo and a soaring Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remastered SBD delivers clear instrument separation and a roomy stage feel, though a brief vocal dip around the 1:11 mark is noted. Musically the show shines – Phil Lesh’s unprecedented New Potato Caboose solo, an emphatic Dark Star, and vibrant renditions of The Other One, Dupree’s Diamond Blues and Doin’ That Rag make it a must‑listen early‑1969 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (mostly 5★) and enthusiastic comments on both the music and the soundboard quality outweigh only minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Excellent stage imaging and instrument clarity after Charlie Miller’s fix; a brief mix change at ~1:11 lowers vocal presence, and overall vocals sit slightly low in the early part of the set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set launches explosively with Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → New Potato Caboose, then eases into song‑driven numbers; second set is tight and features a focused 20‑minute Dark Star that showcases the band’s burgeoning space‑rock prowess.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s black Les Paul tone is praised; occasional vocal mix dip noted, but his guitar work and leads (e.g., into Dupree’s) are highlighted as strong.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly lauded for an unprecedented, extended bass solo on New Potato Caboose and overall clear, pronounced presence throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals described as initially under‑mixed then improving; his rhythm work is solid but not a focal point in reviews.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboards are called “nicely placed” with delicate, nuanced playing that complements the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s maracas and Bill’s primal drumming are noted for their intensity and classic 1968‑69 feel, especially during Dark Star and The Other One.
